opening: Spring 278 BCE, before Pyrrhus' Sicilian expedition; a scenario convention without an invented calendar day.

polybius-1.role: Later ancient testimony, 1.7-8: Mamertines, Messana and the Campanian garrison at Rhegion; not a contemporary border survey.

polybius-2.role: Later ancient testimony, 2.41: re-formation of the Achaean League and subsequent accession of Aegium.

spring-sicily.role: Later ancient fragments, 22.7-10: changing Sicilian regimes and Pyrrhus' intervention. Akragas-Syracuse is the explicitly approved gameplay aggregation.

athens-kallias.role: Inscription of 270/269 recalling earlier events. Civic Athens and Macedonian military positions are distinct; exact Piraeus chronology is qualified.

memnon.role: Later ancient account preserved in an epitome: distinct Bosporus communities, Bithynian politics and Galatian movements.

spring-convention.role: Modern concordance to ancient sources. Spring pre-expedition timing is an approved scenario convention, not a claim of an exact day.

iranica-colchis.role: Modern scholarly regional geography; distinguish western Colchis from eastern Iberia.

iranica-yuezhi.role: Modern scholarship places the migration into Bactria in the second century BCE. Existing western starting ownership is withdrawn, not the faction identity.

strabo-gaul.role: Later testimony for regional associations. Transfers in Gaul are bounded gameplay reconstructions, not verified 278 BCE frontiers.

samarobriva.role: Modern scholarly gazetteer: Samarobriva Ambianorum. The existing Belgae faction is the approved broader regional approximation.

livy-neapolis.role: Later ancient testimony, Livy 8.26.6-7: Neapolis' treaty relationship. Roman colour represents an allied sphere, not uniform direct administration.

cultureChanges.name: Irish regional communities
cultureChanges.note: Indigenous Irish communities. Precise early linguistic and political affiliations remain uncertain; Brittonic is not imposed.

cultureChanges.name: Venetic
cultureChanges.note: Regional Venetic identity, distinguished from a generic Italic language assignment.

cultureChanges.name: Daunian / northern Iapygian
cultureChanges.note: Regional grouping; no claim that every Daunian spoke Messapic.

cultureChanges.name: Northwestern Iberian communities
cultureChanges.note: Geographic parent grouping, not a uniform language or Celtiberian identity.

cultureChanges.name: Vaccaean
cultureChanges.note: Separate regional identity; not automatically Celtiberian.

cultureChanges.name: Vettonian
cultureChanges.note: Separate regional identity; not automatically Celtiberian.

cultureChanges.name: Lusitanian
cultureChanges.note: Regional identity; precise linguistic classification is not settled here.

cultureChanges.name: Vasconian regional communities
cultureChanges.note: Regional classification; no uniform Iberian language or later political frontier is inferred.

cultureChanges.name: Armenian
cultureChanges.note: Armenian regional identity and Iranian dynastic influences are distinct concepts.

cultureChanges.name: Colchian
cultureChanges.note: Regional classification; a uniform ethnic or linguistic boundary is not asserted.

cultureChanges.name: Kartlian / eastern Iberian
cultureChanges.note: Eastern Iberian regional political identity; early dynastic chronology remains qualified.

cultureChanges.name: Minaean
cultureChanges.note: Distinct South Arabian kingdom and cultural tradition.

cultureChanges.name: Sabaean
cultureChanges.note: Distinct South Arabian kingdom and cultural tradition.

cultureChanges.name: Hadramitic
cultureChanges.note: Distinct South Arabian kingdom and cultural tradition.

cultureChanges.name: Qatabanian
cultureChanges.note: Distinct South Arabian kingdom and cultural tradition.

cultureChanges.name: Classification under review
cultureChanges.note: A Scythian identity is not asserted; no replacement ethnicity is invented.

patches.note: Mamertine control of Messana. The Campanian controlling community and the Greek civic/urban context remain distinct. No First Punic War trigger.
Approved Akragas-Syracuse gameplay aggregation; distinct local government is retained in historical context. Pyrrhus has not yet taken command in Sicily.
Greek Neapolis in the Roman allied sphere. Political colour simplifies a treaty relationship; it does not assert direct Roman administration or Roman cultural identity.
Athenian civic authority distinguished from Macedonian military positions. District boundary is a scenario approximation.
Macedonian garrison reconstruction. Exact recovery chronology is debated; civic culture remains Greek.
Aegium precedes its later accession to the renewed Achaean League. Macedonian garrison control is the bounded starting approximation.
Chalcedon remains separate from Byzantion on the Asian shore. The city point is unchanged.
Later Carnutian association guides this explicitly approximate 278 allocation.
Ambianian community represented through the existing broader Belgic grouping; no new Ambiani faction or documented unified Belgic state is invented.
Bituriges Vivisci association represented through the existing Bituriges record. This is not a claim that Vivisci and Cubi formed one documented 278 state.
Volcaean association is a regional starting approximation; this does not assign Tolosa to an Anatolian migration marker.
Targeted western Sicilian political coverage. Physical coastline and settlement position are unchanged.
Restore political coverage at the existing Greek civic centre; no blanket ownership of colonial connections.
Bounded coverage correction around the existing Bosporan civic centre, not a movement of its researched location.
Restore the existing Heracleote point to its own political community. District extent is approximate.
